name: Sitka National Historical Park
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Sitka National Historical Park in Sitka, Alaska, is the oldest federally designated park in Alaska, established as a public park in 1890 and redesignated a national monument in 1910 and a national historical park in 1972. The park preserves the site of the 1804 Battle of Sitka — the last major armed resistance by the Tlingit people against Russian colonization in Alaska. The battle occurred when Tlingit warriors defended a wooden fort (the Shís'gi Noow) against a combined Russian and Aleut force; after several days of fighting, the Tlingit withdrew in a strategic retreat. The park also houses the Southeast Alaska Indian Cultural Center, where Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian artists practice and demonstrate traditional carving, weaving, and other art forms, and maintains a renowned collection of totem poles along a temperate rainforest trail.
